    Raup-Crick dissimilarity against a null model

    Source: R/beta-uniqueness.R
    beta_raup_crick.Rd

    Pairwise dissimilarity that controls for differences in richness, using the probabilistic null model of Chase et al. (2011). For each pair of sites, species are drawn at random for both sites, keeping their observed richness and drawing each species with probability proportional to the number of sites it occupies in the group. The observed number of shared species is compared with this null distribution. Values near 1 mean fewer shared species than chance (deterministic divergence), near -1 more than chance (convergence), and near 0 a composition no different from random assembly.

    Usage

    beta_raup_crick(
  data,
  site = site,
  species = species,
  abundance = NULL,
  nsim = 999,
  .by = NULL
)

    Arguments

    data

    A data frame in long format, with one row per record.

    site, species

    <tidy-select> The column holding site identifiers and the column holding species names.

    abundance

    <tidy-select> The column holding counts. If NULL (the default), a column called abundance is used when present, otherwise every row counts as one individual.

    nsim

    Number of null communities per pair.

    .by

    <tidy-select> Optional grouping columns, kept in the output. Grouped data frames are also respected.

    Value

    A tibble with the grouping columns, site_1, site_2, shared (observed shared species), null_mean, raup_crick (from -1 to 1, Chase et al. 2011) and probability (the same on a 0 to 1 scale). Ties between the null and observed counts count half, as in Chase et al. (2011), so probability lies between the two versions of vegan::raupcrick() (chase = TRUE counts no ties, chase = FALSE all of them).

    References

    Chase, J. M., Kraft, N. J. B., Smith, K. G., Vellend, M. and Inouye, B. D. (2011). Using null models to disentangle variation in community dissimilarity from variation in alpha-diversity. Ecosphere, 2, art24. doi:10.1890/ES10-00117.1

    Examples

    set.seed(1)
beta_raup_crick(png_ants, .by = season, nsim = 199)
#> # A tibble: 20 × 7
#>    season site_1 site_2 shared null_mean raup_crick probability
